Glossary
Anemia Low blood hemoglobin levels, mostly usually caused by iron deﬁciency.
Child Health Days Outreach strategy allowing high coverage of interventions such as vaccines and supplements during
quarterly or six monthly extension of speciﬁc services into villages on set days.
Micronutrient supplementation The provision of micronutrients as pills, capsules, or syrups, for periodic consumption.
Randomized controlled trials Experiments carried out with a control or placebo group that is randomly and blindly assigned.
Therapeutic supplements Supplements with a dose larger than the daily requirement, used to treat micronutrient deﬁciency.
Introduction
Micronutrient supplementation is the distribution of specially formulated preparations of one or more micronutrients, usually in
the form of a pill, a capsule, or sirup. It is often described as a ‘short-term’ option and a ‘medical’ approach and considered more
appropriate for the treatment of severe micronutrient deﬁciencies in those most affected than to prevent deﬁciencies in whole pop-
